groups.title: Tablet (D40600ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills with shivering, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; if you are 30 weeks or more pregnant; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if you have an allergic constitution; if you have liver, kidney, heart or thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure or gastric or duodenal ulcer; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 4.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen, an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like), an antitussive-expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative, or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine). Do not take this medicine if you have stopped taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) within the past 2 weeks. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are being given a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant or a steroid. Consult a pharmacist if you are being given barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, or, rarely, signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome, with high fever, rash and reddening of the skin and severe burn-like blisters on the skin of the whole body or on the mouth or eye membranes), acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, asthma, general lassitude, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes) or interstitial pneumonia (cough, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, fever) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.usage: Adolescents and adults aged 12 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; or if you have severe renal failure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney impairment or hypoproteinaemia, or if you are pregnant.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with a phosphate, a calcium salt, an oral tetracycline preparation or an antacid. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with an antialdosterone medicine or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If red spots, diarrhoea, cardiac arrest, reduced central nervous system function, gastrointestinal disturbance, digestive disturbance, upper abdominal pain, nausea, low blood pressure, pulmonary oedema or vomiting occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (105203ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for neutralising acid and improving symptoms in gastric and duodenal ulcer, gastritis, excess stomach acid, heartburn, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain and acid eructation (sour belching).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 12 years and older: chew and take 1 g per dose by mouth, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes to 1 hour after meals. If needed, 1 further dose may be taken before bedtime.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have Alzheimer's disease; if you have haemorrhoids; if you have fluid retention (swelling); if you have pre-eclampsia; if you have diarrhoea; or if you have undiagnosed bleeding in the digestive tract.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have kidney impairment; if you are physically weak; if you are on a low-phosphorus diet; if you have a problem with digestion and absorption; if you are an older person; if you have symptoms of bleeding in the digestive tract such as vomiting of blood or black stools; or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

If symptoms do not improve after about 2 weeks of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian.

Do not take it together with a tetracycline antibiotic. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic (NSAID), an ulcer medicine, a digitalis preparation, chlorpromazine, lansoprazole, prednisolone, penicillin, a quinolone, an iron (Fe) salt preparation or a salicylate.

If constipation or diarrhoea occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (199501ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint disease), ankylosing spondylitis, tendinitis, acute gout, dysmenorrhoea, bursitis, skeletal muscle disorders (sprain, contusion, injury, lumbosacral pain), pain after surgery, migraine and pain after tooth extraction.
groups.usage: For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis and ankylosing spondylitis, adults: take 1 to 2 tablets (275 to 550 mg) per dose, 2 times in 1 day (every 12 hours). For acute gout: take 3 tablets (825 mg) as the first dose, then 1 tablet (275 mg) at intervals of 8 hours until the attack settles. For skeletal muscle disorders, pain after surgery, pain after tooth extraction, dysmenorrhoea, tendinitis and bursitis: take 2 tablets (550 mg) as the first dose, then 1 tablet (275 mg) at intervals of 6 to 8 hours, without exceeding a total of 5 tablets (1375 mg) in 1 day. For migraine: take 3 tablets (825 mg) as the first dose; if needed, 1 to 2 further tablets (275 to 550 mg) may be taken in 1 day, 30 minutes after the first dose. Do not exceed a total of 5 tablets (1375 mg) in 1 day.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have peptic ulcer, a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency, severe kidney impairment or severe high blood pressure; if you have hypersensitivity to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic; if you have or have had asthma, rhinitis, nasal polyps, urticaria or an allergic reaction caused by aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic (including COX-2 inhibitors); if it is for the treatment of pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass graft surgery; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you may be pregnant; if the user is a child; if you are an older person; if you have had peptic ulcer or a blood disorder; if you have a tendency to bleed; if you have or have had liver impairment or kidney impairment; if you have impaired heart function, high blood pressure or bronchial asthma; or if you have systemic lupus erythematosus or mixed connective tissue disease.

Do not take it together with another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic or naproxen derivative, aspirin or high-dose methotrexate. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with a hydantoin antiepileptic, a sulfonamide, a sulfonylurea blood-glucose-lowering medicine, propranolol or another beta blocker, an ACE inhibitor (captopril and the like), a loop or thiazide diuretic, probenecid or lithium.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: PIE syndrome (pulmonary infiltration with eosinophilia: fever, wheezing, cough and sputum); urticaria; occasionally hypersensitivity symptoms such as rash or itching; vomiting of blood, gastrointestinal bleeding, peptic ulcer or perforation; aseptic meningitis (severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or disturbance of consciousness); eczema, sweating, purpura, photosensitivity, hair loss, reddening of the skin, necrotic lysis, erythema multiforme, exfoliative dermatitis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis, urticaria, epidermolysis bullosa, drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms, fixed drug eruption; rarely blood disorders such as agranulocytosis, eosinophilia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia or reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time).

Occasionally stomach discomfort, stomach pain, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, indigestion, heartburn, diarrhoea, constipation or stomatitis, and rarely abdominal distension, black stools, thirst, raised GOT or GPT, jaundice, hepatitis, kidney impairment, nephritis, blood in the urine, high blood potassium, interstitial nephritis, nephrotic syndrome, renal papillary necrosis, protein in the urine, renal failure, ringing in the ears, hearing disturbance, visual disturbance, swelling, difficulty breathing, palpitations, muscle weakness, congestive heart failure, eosinophilic pneumonia, an anaphylactoid reaction, menstrual disturbance, chills with fever, vasculitis, high blood sugar or low blood sugar may occur.

For a child weighing 30 kg or less, do not exceed 25 mL (300 mg) in 1 day. Refer to the approved product information for the recommended dose for each age group.

If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, peptic ulcer, a severe blood disorder, liver impairment, kidney impairment, cardiac insufficiency or high blood pressure; if you have or have had bronchial asthma, or asthma, urticaria or an allergy caused by aspirin or another anti-inflammatory analgesic; if it is for the treatment of pain before or after coronary artery bypass surgery; or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have hypersensitivity, peptic ulcer, a blood disorder, a tendency to bleed, liver impairment, kidney impairment, cardiac insufficiency or high blood pressure; if you have systemic lupus erythematosus, mixed connective tissue disease, ulcerative colitis, stomach cancer or Crohn's disease; if you are an older person or the user is a child; or if you take low-dose aspirin to prevent myocardial infarction or stroke.

Do not use it together with another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic, aspirin or high-dose methotrexate. Consult a pharmacist if you use it together with a glucocorticoid, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, a sulfonylurea, a diuretic with an antihypertensive, an ACE inhibitor, furosemide, lithium, low-dose methotrexate or a coumarin anticoagulant (warfarin and the like).

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rarely shock (difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure and the like), chest discomfort, chills, difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure; aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia, agranulocytosis, granulocytopenia, leukopenia; gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis; Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency; acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis; triggering of an asthma attack, urticaria, eczema, purpura; occasionally rash or itching; rarely loss of vision or visual disturbance such as scotoma; aseptic meningitis; acute renal failure, reduced urine output, blood in the urine, protein in the urine, raised BUN or blood creatinine, or high blood potassium.

Occasionally loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort or swelling around the eye sockets, rarely jaundice, raised GOT, GPT or ALP, hearing loss, ringing in the ears, taste disturbance, a fall or rise in blood pressure, palpitations, reduced urine volume, generalised oedema with breathlessness or lassitude or acute pulmonary oedema, and very rarely thirst, stomatitis, abdominal distension, constipation, malaise, fever or nosebleed may occur; if these occur, consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Reducing fever caused by an acute upper respiratory tract infection
summaryTable.Choosing a product: Products with the same generic-name code (142334ASY) share the same ingredient, strength and dosage form. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the brand name.
summaryTable.Ask the pharmacist: Ask the pharmacist in the store first if any of the cautions above apply to you.
